newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IMF's Camdessus says Thai supervision lax -paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus says Thai supervision lax -paper.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) chief Michel Camdessus said the Thai authorities had contributed to their current troubles by failing to maintain tight supervision and discipline, a Hong Kong newspaper reported on Friday.
The English-language South China Morning Post said the IMF was holding talks with Thai officials and steps were being taken to rebuild confidence in the financial sector.
"Thailand is in a difficult phase after a very remarkable period of development," the newspaper quoted Camdessus as saying.
"Thailand has allowed too high a balance of payments to develop and its financial institutions have not been maintained in sufficiently tight supervision and discipline," he said.
"It is now in a period of adjustment and the measures (being taken) are sound."
He said lesson learned from the Mexican peso crisis would be applied in the region as East Asia became increasingly more important in the global financial system.
He said Hong Kong was on the shortlist as the centre for the IMF's new Asian office and key personnel, including Asian regional director Kunio Saito, would be moved to the region.
"Strengthening surveillence will particularly apply to these Asian business centres."
"One must be there to encourage or be ready to intervene with all means, hopefully with the cooperation of others."
Camdessus said the IMF needed to be "closer to the people, closer to the regional meetings and closer to the regional organisations."
